A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same data-structure discovery framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original nearest-neighbor and streaming frequency-estimation experiments, including architectural ablations and analyses of learned structures.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds real-data benchmarks, hashing comparisons, seed-variability plots, attention ablations, and throughput measurements.

M1.justification: v2 adds a linear-attention Performer alternative to the data-processing transformer, evaluated in Appendix D.1. The core permutation-learning and query mechanisms remain intact. Shared query weights and reduced-delta CountMinSketch already appeared in v1; the newly specified CNN layers are additional documentation.

E1.justification: v2 adds FashionMNIST and SIFT nearest-neighbor evaluation and tests modified CountMinSketch on CAIDA network traffic. These substantially broaden the represented data beyond v1's synthetic distributions and constructed MNIST tasks. Earlier Zipfian, extra-space, and MNIST frequency-estimation experiments remain in the appendices.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ITQ, KMeans, and NeuralLSH to the existing hypersphere comparison, which previously used LSH and model ablations. The retained three-digit MNIST experiment gains a label-space oracle hashing comparator, labeled LSH, alongside binary search (Figure 19). These are substantive additions to evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: The reported maximum NN training budget changes from four million to two million steps; this does not establish that retained results were rerun. New protocols include FashionMNIST PCA preprocessing, 16-partition learned-hashing comparisons, CAIDA memory/delta sweeps, and throughput testing across dataset sizes, lookup budgets, and depths. SIFT dimensionality remains inconsistent between the 100D prose and Figure 17's 128D label.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled linear-versus-quadratic attention comparisons (Figure 26), a FashionMNIST clustering example (Figure 18), and extensive computational-overhead sensitivity analysis (Appendix D.3). The CAIDA delta/memory sweep expands the investigation of reduced CountMinSketch updates, while v1's synthetic delta-validation plot, Figure 22, is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 adds three-seed plots for the 1D, 2D, and hypersphere experiments, and Appendix D.3 specifies averaging timings over ten trials. The checklist newly identifies bootstrapped confidence intervals. v1 already contains shaded uncertainty bands but does not give corresponding seed counts or a bootstrap explanation.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include E2E accuracies of 67.2% on FashionMNIST and 46.9% on SIFT (Table 1), CAIDA update-delta results (Figure 23), and throughput tables (Appendix D.3). These extend the evidence rather than establish same-setting performance gains over v1. The earlier synthetic CountMinSketch delta-validation curves are absent.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematical formulations for nearest-neighbor search, lookups, hashing, and sketch updates are retained. Neither version provides formal theoretical results or proofs. Appendix C.7's new two-element failure explanation is presented as an informal mechanism hypothesis.

C1.justification: The central claim that constrained end-to-end learning can discover meaningful data structures remains. v2 adds introduction-level claims of competitiveness on FashionMNIST/SIFT and transfer of a learned CountMinSketch insight to a practical dataset (Section 1.2), modestly extending the claimed demonstrated scope.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's scale discussion, v2 explicitly examines neural inference and preprocessing overhead, explains why optimized quadratic attention can outperform linear attention, and discusses a high-skew frequency-estimation failure requiring suitable initialization (Section 5; Appendices C.7 and D). These materially qualify efficiency and the conditions under which learning succeeds.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, the full CNN layer specification, input/output projection details, and fuller training-data and benchmarking documentation. However, v1's synthetic frequency-estimation universe size and Zipfian exponent are no longer specified for that experiment. The repository's actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against neural algorithmic reasoning and neural sketching, including Meta-sketch, Learning to Sketch, and Lego Sketch (Section 4; Appendix C.6). It distinguishes discovery with limited inductive biases from scalable sketching and relates the reduced-update insight to Aamand et al. These are substantive contextual additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, results summary, and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with a broader Discussion section. Zipfian NN results, extra-space experiments, and frequency-estimation implementation details move into reorganized topical appendices. A contents list and conference checklist are also added.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the displays: it combines LSH/MNIST visualizations in Figure 4, rearranges the k-d-tree heatmaps, converts v1's extra-space Figure 8 into Table 2, and adds comparison tables, seed plots, CAIDA figures, attention comparisons, and throughput tables. Numerous retained plots are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The real-data comparisons against learned hashing methods and the CAIDA transfer experiment substantially strengthen v1's limited evidence beyond controlled examples. Runtime measurements, seed checks, fuller research positioning, and explicit failure conditions also make the framework's scope more assessable. These gains outweigh the removed synthetic delta-validation plot and settings, although inconsistencies such as SIFT dimensionality and the reversed CAIDA ratio-axis label reduce reporting precision.
